form.en: old-style poem with lines of mixed length, on an old yuefu ballad title

text_note.zh: 这里用的是现在课本里的通行文字。古籍收录的文字有些不同：“不与秦塞通人烟”一作“乃与秦塞通人烟”；“相钩连”一作“方钩连”；“尚不得过”一作“尚不得”；“攀援”一作“攀缘”；“古木”一作“枯木”；“雄飞雌从”一作“雄飞呼雌”；“凋朱颜”一作“雕朱颜”；“争喧豗”一作“相喧豗”；“砯崖”一作“砅崖”；“其险也如此”一作“其崄也若此”。“猿”“剑”在古籍里写作异体字“猨”“劒”。课本把“蜀道之难，难于上青天”分成两句。
text_note.en: This is the text taught in schools today. Old collections differ in places. Bù yǔ (“never joined”) appears as nǎi yǔ (“only then joined”). Xiāng gōu lián appears as fāng gōu lián. Shàng bù dé guò appears without guò. Gǔ mù (“old trees”) appears as kū mù (“dead trees”). Xióng fēi cí cóng (“the male flies, the female follows”) appears as xióng fēi hū cí (“the male flies, calling the female”). Some other words are written with different but similar characters. Textbooks split the refrain “the road to Shu is so hard, harder than climbing to the blue sky” into two lines.

readings.zh: 读 xī。原本是惊叹声，课本注音 xī。
readings.en: Read xī, as marked in textbooks. It is part of a cry of surprise.
Here it is an exclamation, read xū.

readings.zh: 指险要的地方，读 sài，不读 sāi 或 sè。
readings.en: Meaning a guarded frontier place, it is read sài, not sāi or sè.

readings.zh: 这里是星宿名，读 shēn，不读 cān。
readings.en: Here it is the name of a star group, read shēn, not cān.
Meaning to come back, read huán.

readings.zh: 大声哀叫，读 háo，不读 hào。
readings.en: Meaning to wail, read háo, not hào.

readings.zh: “胡为”就是“为什么”，一般读 wèi；也有人读 wéi。
readings.en: Hú wèi means “why”. It is usually read wèi; some read it wéi.
Meaning morning, read zhāo, not cháo.

glosses.zh: 噫吁嚱：惊叹的声音，相当于“哎呀呀”。据说是蜀地的方言。
glosses.en: yī xū xī: a cry of surprise, like “oh, oh, oh!” It is said to come from the local speech of Shu.

glosses.zh: 危：高。
glosses.en: wēi: high.

glosses.zh: 乎：语气词，表示感叹，相当于“啊”。后面的“哉”也是这样。
glosses.en: hū: a word for exclaiming, like “oh!” The word zāi at the end works the same way.

glosses.zh: 蜀道：从秦地（今陕西一带）进入蜀地（今四川一带）的山路。
glosses.en: shǔ dào: the mountain road from Qin (around today's Shaanxi) into Shu (around today's Sichuan).

glosses.zh: 难于上青天：比登上青天还难。于，比。
glosses.en: nán yú shàng qīng tiān: harder than climbing up to the blue sky. Yú here means “than”.

glosses.zh: 蚕丛及鱼凫：蚕丛和鱼凫，传说中古代蜀国最早的两位国王。及，和。
glosses.en: cán cóng jí yú fú: Cancong and Yufu, two legendary first kings of ancient Shu. Jí means “and”.

glosses.zh: 何茫然：多么模糊不清啊。开国的事太久远了，已经说不清楚。何，多么。
glosses.en: hé máng rán: how dim and unclear! The founding of the kingdom is so long ago that no one can tell the story clearly. Hé here means “how”.

glosses.zh: 尔来：从那时以来。
glosses.en: ěr lái: since that time.

glosses.zh: 四万八千岁：夸张的说法，形容年代非常久远。
glosses.en: sì wàn bā qiān suì: an exaggeration, meaning a very, very long time.

glosses.zh: 秦塞：秦地，今陕西一带。塞，山川险要的地方。
glosses.en: qín sài: the land of Qin, around today's Shaanxi. Sài means a place guarded by mountains and rivers.

glosses.zh: 通人烟：人们来来往往。人烟，人家做饭的炊烟，代指人。
glosses.en: tōng rén yān: for people to come and go. Rén yān, the smoke from kitchen fires, stands for people.

glosses.zh: 西当：在西边对着。当，对着。
glosses.en: xī dāng: facing it on the west. Dāng means to face.

glosses.zh: 太白：太白山，秦岭的主峰，在今陕西。
glosses.en: tài bái: Mount Taibai, the highest peak of the Qinling Mountains, in today's Shaanxi.

glosses.zh: 鸟道：只有鸟才能飞过去的路，形容山又高又险，人走不了。
glosses.en: niǎo dào: a road only birds can use, meaning the mountains are so high and steep that people cannot cross.

glosses.zh: 横绝：横着飞越过去。绝，越过。
glosses.en: héng jué: to fly straight across. Jué means to cross over.

glosses.zh: 峨眉巅：峨眉山的山顶。峨眉山在今四川。
glosses.en: é méi diān: the top of Mount Emei, in today's Sichuan.

glosses.zh: 地崩山摧壮士死：传说秦王答应送五个美女给蜀王，蜀王派五个大力士去接。走到半路，看见一条大蛇钻进山洞，五个人一起拉蛇尾巴，结果山崩了，大力士和美女都被压死。摧，倒塌。
glosses.en: dì bēng shān cuī zhuàng shì sǐ: a legend: the king of Qin promised five beautiful women to the king of Shu, who sent five strong men to fetch them. On the way they saw a huge snake crawl into a cave. The five men pulled its tail together, the mountain fell down, and the strong men and the women were all crushed. Cuī means to collapse.

glosses.zh: 天梯：像通到天上去的梯子一样的陡峭山路。
glosses.en: tiān tī: a steep mountain path like a ladder up to the sky.

glosses.zh: 石栈：栈道，在悬崖上凿洞、插上木头、铺上木板修成的路。
glosses.en: shí zhàn: a plank road: holes are cut in a cliff, beams are fixed in them, and boards are laid on top to make a path.

glosses.zh: 钩连：连接起来。
glosses.en: gōu lián: to link together.

glosses.zh: 六龙回日：神话说太阳神坐着车，由六条龙拉着在天上跑。这里说山太高，连太阳的车到了这里也只好掉头回去。
glosses.en: liù lóng huí rì: in myth, the sun rides across the sky in a carriage pulled by six dragons. Here the mountain is so tall that even the sun's carriage has to turn back.

glosses.zh: 高标：最高的山峰，高得可以当作一个地方的标志。
glosses.en: gāo biāo: the highest peak, so tall it marks the whole region.

glosses.zh: 冲波：互相冲击的波浪。
glosses.en: chōng bō: waves crashing against each other.

glosses.zh: 逆折：水流被挡住，倒转回旋。
glosses.en: nì zhé: water blocked and turned back on itself.

glosses.zh: 回川：打着漩涡的河流。
glosses.en: huí chuān: a river full of whirlpools.

glosses.zh: 黄鹤：黄鹄，一种很会高飞的大鸟。
glosses.en: huáng hè: the yellow crane, a big bird that can fly very high.

glosses.zh: 尚不得过：尚且飞不过去。尚，尚且、都还。
glosses.en: shàng bù dé guò: still cannot get across. Shàng means “even so, still”.

glosses.zh: 猿猱：猿猴。猱是一种特别会爬树的猴子。
glosses.en: yuán náo: apes and monkeys. Náo is a monkey that is very good at climbing.

glosses.zh: 度：越过。
glosses.en: dù: to cross.

glosses.zh: 愁攀援：发愁怎么攀爬过去。
glosses.en: chóu pān yuán: worried about how to climb across.

glosses.zh: 青泥：青泥岭，在今甘肃徽县南、陕西略阳北，是进入蜀地的要道。
glosses.en: qīng ní: Qingni Ridge, south of today's Hui County in Gansu and north of Lueyang in Shaanxi, a main road into Shu.

glosses.zh: 盘盘：一圈一圈绕来绕去的样子。
glosses.en: pán pán: winding round and round.

glosses.zh: 百步九折：走一百步就要拐九个弯。
glosses.en: bǎi bù jiǔ zhé: nine turns in every hundred steps.

glosses.zh: 萦：围着……绕。
glosses.en: yíng: to wind around.

glosses.zh: 岩峦：山崖和山峰。
glosses.en: yán luán: cliffs and peaks.

glosses.zh: 扪参历井：参和井是天上两组星星的名字。古人把天上的星区和地上的地方配对，参对着蜀地，井对着秦地。扪，用手摸；历，经过。这里说山高得伸手就能摸到星星。
glosses.en: mén shēn lì jǐng: Shēn and Jǐng are the names of two groups of stars. People of old matched parts of the sky with places on earth: Shēn matched Shu and Jǐng matched Qin. Mén means to touch; lì means to pass by. The mountain is so high you can reach out and touch the stars.

glosses.zh: 仰胁息：抬着头，屏住呼吸，不敢大口喘气。胁息，屏住气。
glosses.en: yǎng xié xī: looking up and holding your breath, too scared to breathe hard. Xié xī means to hold one's breath.

glosses.zh: 抚膺：用手摸着胸口。膺，胸。
glosses.en: fǔ yīng: to press a hand on one's chest. Yīng means chest.

glosses.zh: 坐：空自、只能。
glosses.en: zuò: helplessly, with nothing to do but.

glosses.zh: 君：你，指要到蜀地去的人。
glosses.en: jūn: you, the person heading for Shu.

glosses.zh: 西游：往西去，指进入蜀地。
glosses.en: xī yóu: to travel west, that is, into Shu.

glosses.zh: 畏途：让人害怕的路。
glosses.en: wèi tú: a road that makes people afraid.

glosses.zh: 巉岩：又高又陡的山岩。
glosses.en: chán yán: tall, sharp, steep rocks.

glosses.zh: 但见：只看见。
glosses.en: dàn jiàn: all one sees is.

glosses.zh: 号：大声哀叫。
glosses.en: háo: to wail loudly.

glosses.zh: 古木：老树。
glosses.en: gǔ mù: old trees.

glosses.zh: 雄飞雌从：雄鸟在前面飞，雌鸟在后面跟着。
glosses.en: xióng fēi cí cóng: the male bird flies ahead and the female follows.

glosses.zh: 子规：杜鹃鸟。传说它是古代蜀王杜宇死后变的，叫声很悲伤。
glosses.en: zǐ guī: the cuckoo. Legend says it is the spirit of Du Yu, an ancient king of Shu, and its call sounds very sad.

glosses.zh: 愁空山：叫声在空寂的山里回荡，让整座山都好像充满了忧愁。
glosses.en: chóu kōng shān: its call echoes through the empty mountains and fills them with sorrow.

glosses.zh: 凋朱颜：红润的脸色一下子变得憔悴，就是吓得变了脸色。凋，使……衰败；朱颜，红润的脸。
glosses.en: diāo zhū yán: the rosy face turns pale and worn, that is, people go white with fear. Diāo means to wither; zhū yán means a rosy face.

glosses.zh: 去天不盈尺：离天不到一尺。去，离；盈，满。
glosses.en: qù tiān bù yíng chǐ: less than a foot from the sky. Qù means away from; yíng means to fill, to reach.

glosses.zh: 倚：靠着。
glosses.en: yǐ: to lean against.

glosses.zh: 绝壁：像刀切过一样陡的山崖。
glosses.en: jué bì: a cliff as steep as if cut with a knife.

glosses.zh: 飞湍：飞奔的急流。
glosses.en: fēi tuān: rushing rapids.

glosses.zh: 瀑流：瀑布。
glosses.en: pù liú: waterfalls.

glosses.zh: 争喧豗：争着发出轰隆隆的巨响。喧豗，水流撞击的轰鸣声。
glosses.en: zhēng xuān huī: compete in making a roaring noise. Xuān huī is the thunder of crashing water.

glosses.zh: 砯崖转石：水冲击着山崖，推着石头翻滚。砯，水冲击石头的声音，这里当动词用。
glosses.en: pīng yá zhuǎn shí: the water pounds the cliffs and rolls the rocks along. Pīng is the sound of water striking stone, used here as a verb.

glosses.zh: 万壑雷：千山万谷都响起像打雷一样的声音。壑，山谷。
glosses.en: wàn hè léi: ten thousand valleys roar like thunder. Hè means a valley.

glosses.zh: 其险也如此：这里的险要竟然到了这个地步。
glosses.en: qí xiǎn yě rú cǐ: the danger here is as great as this.

glosses.zh: 嗟：唉，叹气的声音。
glosses.en: jiē: alas, a sigh.

glosses.zh: 尔：你。
glosses.en: ěr: you.

glosses.zh: 远道之人：从远方来的人。
glosses.en: yuǎn dào zhī rén: a person from far away.

glosses.zh: 胡为乎来哉：为什么要到这里来呢？胡为，为什么。
glosses.en: hú wèi hū lái zāi: why ever come here? Hú wèi means why.

glosses.zh: 剑阁：剑门关，在今四川剑阁县北，是进入蜀地的大门。两边的山壁像剑一样直立。
glosses.en: jiàn gé: Jianmen Pass, north of today's Jian'ge County in Sichuan, the gateway into Shu. The cliffs on both sides stand up straight like swords.

glosses.zh: 峥嵘：山势高而险的样子。
glosses.en: zhēng róng: high and rugged.

glosses.zh: 崔嵬：山高大雄伟的样子。
glosses.en: cuī wéi: tall and towering.

glosses.zh: 一夫当关：一个人守住关口。当，守着。
glosses.en: yī fū dāng guān: one man guards the pass. Dāng means to hold.

glosses.zh: 万夫莫开：一万个人也攻不进去。莫，不能。
glosses.en: wàn fū mò kāi: ten thousand men cannot break through. Mò means cannot.

glosses.zh: 所守：守关的人。
glosses.en: suǒ shǒu: those who guard the pass.

glosses.zh: 或匪亲：如果不是可靠的自己人。或，如果；匪，同“非”，不是。
glosses.en: huò fěi qīn: if they are not trusted friends. Huò here means if; fěi means not.

glosses.zh: 化为狼与豺：就会变成豺狼一样作乱的人。豺，一种像狼的猛兽。
glosses.en: huà wéi láng yǔ chái: they will turn into wolves and jackals, that is, rebels. Chái is a jackal, a fierce wolf-like beast.

glosses.zh: 朝：早晨。
glosses.en: zhāo: in the morning.

glosses.zh: 避：躲开。
glosses.en: bì: to hide from.

glosses.zh: 夕：傍晚。
glosses.en: xī: in the evening.

glosses.zh: 长蛇：大蛇。
glosses.en: cháng shé: great snakes.

glosses.zh: 吮：吸。
glosses.en: shǔn: to suck.

glosses.zh: 杀人如麻：杀的人多得像乱麻一样，数也数不清。
glosses.en: shā rén rú má: killing people as many as tangled hemp threads, too many to count.

glosses.zh: 锦城：锦官城，就是今天的成都。
glosses.en: jǐn chéng: the City of Brocade, today's Chengdu.

glosses.zh: 虽云乐：虽然说是个快乐的地方。云，说。
glosses.en: suī yún lè: though people say it is a happy place. Yún means to say.

glosses.zh: 还家：回家。
glosses.en: huán jiā: to go home.

glosses.zh: 侧身：侧着身子。
glosses.en: cè shēn: turning sideways.

glosses.zh: 长咨嗟：长长地叹气。咨嗟，叹息。
glosses.en: cháng zī jiē: to sigh long and deep. Zī jiē means to sigh.

translation.zh: 哎呀呀！
translation.en: Oh, oh, oh!

translation.zh: 多么高啊，多么险啊！
translation.en: How high, how steep!

translation.zh: 蜀道的难走，
translation.en: The road to Shu is so hard,

translation.zh: 比登上青天还难！
translation.en: harder than climbing to the blue sky!

translation.zh: 蚕丛和鱼凫两位古王，
translation.en: Cancong and Yufu, the ancient kings,

translation.zh: 他们开国的事多么遥远模糊！
translation.en: how dim and far away is the founding of their land!

translation.zh: 从那时到现在已有四万八千年，
translation.en: For forty-eight thousand years since then,

translation.zh: 蜀地和秦地之间一直没有人来往。
translation.en: no one came and went between Shu and Qin.

translation.zh: 西边对着太白山，只有一条鸟才飞得过的路，
translation.en: To the west stands Mount Taibai, with only a path for birds,

translation.zh: 可以一直飞越到峨眉山顶。
translation.en: that flies straight across to the top of Mount Emei.

translation.zh: 直到山崩地裂，五位壮士被压死，
translation.en: Then the earth shook, the mountain fell, and the strong men died,

translation.zh: 此后高入云天的山路和悬崖上的栈道才连接起来。
translation.en: and only after that were sky-high ladders and cliff-side plank roads linked together.

translation.zh: 上面有连太阳神的六龙车都只好掉头的高峰，
translation.en: Above rise peaks so high that the sun's six-dragon carriage must turn back,

translation.zh: 下面有波浪冲击、倒转回旋的河流。
translation.en: below run rivers whose crashing waves twist back in whirlpools.

translation.zh: 善于高飞的黄鹤都还飞不过去，
translation.en: Even the high-flying yellow crane cannot get across,

translation.zh: 猿猴想翻过去也发愁没处攀爬。
translation.en: and apes and monkeys who want to cross worry how to climb.

translation.zh: 青泥岭的山路多么曲折，
translation.en: How the road on Qingni Ridge winds round and round,

translation.zh: 一百步就要绕着山岩拐九个弯。
translation.en: nine turns in every hundred steps, wrapped around the cliffs!

translation.zh: 伸手能摸到参星井星，仰着头不敢喘气，
translation.en: You touch the stars Shen and Jing, look up, and hold your breath,

translation.zh: 只能用手按着胸口，坐下来长长叹气。
translation.en: then press your chest and sit down with a long, helpless sigh.

translation.zh: 请问你西去蜀地，什么时候才回来？
translation.en: I ask you: going west, when will you come back?

translation.zh: 这条可怕的路上，陡峭的山岩根本没法攀登。
translation.en: On this fearful road the sharp cliffs cannot be climbed.

translation.zh: 只看见鸟儿在老树上悲伤地哀叫，
translation.en: All you see are sad birds wailing in old trees,

translation.zh: 雄鸟飞在前，雌鸟跟在后，在林间盘旋。
translation.en: the male ahead, the female behind, circling through the woods.

translation.zh: 又听见杜鹃在月夜里啼叫，
translation.en: And you hear the cuckoo crying under the night moon,

translation.zh: 叫声让空寂的山里充满忧愁。
translation.en: filling the empty mountains with sorrow.

translation.zh: 蜀道的难走，
translation.en: The road to Shu is so hard,

translation.zh: 比登上青天还难，
translation.en: harder than climbing to the blue sky,

translation.zh: 让人一听说就吓得变了脸色！
translation.en: that anyone who hears of it turns pale!

translation.zh: 连绵的山峰离天不到一尺，
translation.en: The linked peaks are less than a foot from the sky,

translation.zh: 干枯的松树倒挂着，靠在陡峭的山崖上。
translation.en: and dead pines hang upside down against sheer cliffs.

translation.zh: 飞奔的急流和瀑布争着发出轰响，
translation.en: Rapids and waterfalls roar as if racing each other,

translation.zh: 冲击山崖、推动石头，千山万谷响起雷声。
translation.en: pounding the cliffs and rolling the rocks till ten thousand valleys thunder.

translation.zh: 这里的险要竟然到了这个地步，
translation.en: So dangerous is this place —

translation.zh: 唉，你这远道而来的人，为什么要到这里来呢？
translation.en: alas, you traveler from far away, why ever have you come?

translation.zh: 剑门关高大险峻，
translation.en: Jianmen Pass towers high and steep.

translation.zh: 一个人守住关口，
translation.en: If one man holds the pass,

translation.zh: 一万个人也攻不进来。
translation.en: ten thousand men cannot break through.

translation.zh: 守关的人如果不是可靠的人，
translation.en: If its guards are not men you can trust,

translation.zh: 就会变成豺狼一样的叛贼。
translation.en: they will turn into wolves and jackals.

translation.zh: 早晨要躲避猛虎，
translation.en: In the morning you hide from fierce tigers,

translation.zh: 傍晚要躲避大蛇。
translation.en: in the evening you hide from great snakes.

translation.zh: 它们磨着牙，吸着血，
translation.en: They grind their teeth and suck blood,

translation.zh: 杀的人多得像乱麻。
translation.en: killing people beyond counting.

translation.zh: 成都虽说是个快乐的地方，
translation.en: Though Chengdu is called a happy place,

translation.zh: 还不如早点回家。
translation.en: it is better to go home early.

translation.zh: 蜀道的难走，
translation.en: The road to Shu is so hard,

translation.zh: 比登上青天还难，
translation.en: harder than climbing to the blue sky.

translation.zh: 我侧着身子向西望去，不停地长声叹息。
translation.en: I turn sideways, gaze west, and sigh and sigh.

background.zh: 《蜀道难》是一个乐府旧题，就是古代就有的歌曲题目，前人用它写过蜀道的艰险。一般认为这首诗写在唐玄宗天宝初年李白在长安的时候，一说写于更早的开元年间。据唐人孟棨《本事诗》记载，李白到长安后，贺知章读了这首诗，惊叹不已，称他是“谪仙人”，意思是从天上被贬到人间的神仙。至于为什么写这首诗，说法很多：一说是送朋友入蜀，一说是暗中批评当时的政局，一说只是借古题描写蜀道的险。
background.en: “The Hard Road to Shu” is an old yuefu title, a song title used by earlier poets to describe the dangerous roads into Shu. The poem is usually dated to the early Tianbao years of Emperor Xuanzong, when Li Bai was in Chang'an; another view dates it earlier, to the Kaiyuan years. According to the Tang book Benshi Shi by Meng Qi, when Li Bai came to Chang'an, He Zhizhang read this poem, was amazed, and called him “an immortal banished from heaven”. Why Li Bai wrote it is debated: one view says it was to see off a friend going to Shu, another that it hinted at the politics of the time, and another that he simply used the old title to describe the road.

author_note.zh: 李白（701—762），字太白，号青莲居士，唐代伟大的浪漫主义诗人，被称为“诗仙”。他少年时在蜀地长大，二十多岁才离开家乡，到各地漫游。他熟悉蜀地的高山大河，又特别会想象和夸张，所以能把蜀道写得这样惊心动魄。
author_note.en: Li Bai (701–762), also called Taibai, was a great Tang poet of wild imagination, known as the Immortal of Poetry. He grew up in Shu and left home in his twenties to travel across the land. He knew the high mountains and great rivers of Shu well, and he loved bold imagination and exaggeration, so he could make the road to Shu feel thrilling and terrifying.

appreciation.zh: 这首诗像一场惊险的山中旅行。一开头就是三声“哎呀呀”，接着喊出“蜀道之难，难于上青天”，这句话在诗里出现了三次，像歌里反复唱的副歌。诗人先讲古老的传说：五个壮士拉蛇，山崩地裂，才开出路来。再写山有多高：太阳的车要掉头，黄鹤飞不过，猴子也发愁，人走在上面能摸到星星。然后写声音：悲鸟哀叫，杜鹃夜啼，急流像打雷。最后写剑门关，一个人守住，一万个人也攻不进来，守关的人要是变坏，比猛虎长蛇还可怕。诗句忽长忽短，就像山路一会儿上一会儿下。读完它，你会觉得自己也刚从这条路上走过一遍，心还在怦怦跳。
appreciation.en: This poem is like a thrilling mountain journey. It opens with three cries of “oh!” and then shouts, “The road to Shu is so hard, harder than climbing to the blue sky!” That line comes back three times, like the chorus of a song. First the poet tells old legends: five strong men pulled a snake, the mountain fell, and only then was a road opened. Then he shows how high the mountains are: the sun's carriage must turn back, the crane cannot fly over, the monkeys worry, and walkers can touch the stars. Then come the sounds: sad birds wailing, the cuckoo crying at night, rapids roaring like thunder. Last comes Jianmen Pass, where one man can hold off ten thousand, and where bad guards would be worse than tigers and snakes. The lines grow long and short, just as the road climbs and drops. When you finish, you feel you have just walked that road yourself, with your heart still pounding.
